goal: Test whether stronger causal worker networking can reduce broadcast overhead without materially losing affected-branch closure under stale topology, message loss and ack loss.
hypothesis: Dual relevance projection (ClayGraph + UnifiedDB) with bounded ack/redelivery, idempotent application and periodic anti-entropy reconciliation preserves affected-branch closure at lower fanout than unconditional nine-branch broadcast.
counterhypothesis: Full broadcast is materially more robust; topology staleness makes targeted routing unsafe or reconciliation overhead erases any communication saving.

design.important_model_limit: Ground-truth affected sets are generated from a fixed synthetic dependency graph derived from current branch-interface structure. This is not a live UnifiedDB/ClayGraph runtime and cannot establish production routing correctness.

runtime_metadata.measurement_clock: Python in-process counters; wall-clock performance not claimed

single_projection_ack.conclusion: COUNTERHYPOTHESIS_PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED: ack/redelivery fixes transport loss but not stale relevance topology.

dual_projection_ack_hot_path.duplicate_application_note: Idempotent application was modeled by pulse id; duplicates could be delivered but did not re-apply state.

supported: Single relevance projection is not robust enough under modeled topology staleness.
Independent dual relevance projections materially reduce modeled topology-miss risk.
Ack/redelivery addresses transport loss but must be paired with idempotent application.
Periodic anti-entropy reconciliation can recover residual misses with less modeled fanout than unconditional broadcast.
not_supported_or_not_measured: No Ubuntu/Hostinger latency, CPU, RAM, filesystem or Git contention measurement.
No proof that current UnifiedDB and ClayGraph projections fail independently in production.
No claim that 25 events is the correct reconciliation period.
interpretation.next_falsifier: Implement a minimal versioned pulse/ack/replan projection against current dynamic_work_runtime_v2.py and inject stale epochs, duplicate event files, missed sync, crash/restart and conflicting work revisions. Compare against current WorkEvent baseline on the verified Ubuntu runner.
